subject.title: RFC: Period-based popularity for publishers, skills, and plugins

question: Should ClawHub implement one shared Weekly/Monthly/All time popularity contract across publishers, skills, and plugins now, and which scoring, attribution, backfill, and retention semantics should V1 use?
rationale: Current main has partial seven-day trending, but the missing work affects public discovery semantics and stored analytics data across multiple entity families.

options.title: Approve shared temporal foundation first
options.body: Build package and publisher period rollups, monthly leaderboards, snapshot-pinned cursors, and docs/spec coverage before adding visible tabs.

options.title: Limit UI to existing trending
options.body: Expose only the already-supported seven-day skill/plugin trending behavior and avoid publisher period tabs until publisher rollups exist.

options.title: Defer the RFC
options.body: Keep existing all-time, recommended, and trending browse surfaces unchanged until discovery work is prioritized against other ClawHub roadmap items.

recommendation.title: Approve shared temporal foundation first
recommendation.body: Build package and publisher period rollups, monthly leaderboards, snapshot-pinned cursors, and docs/spec coverage before adding visible tabs.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the RFC and have merged history on the creator/publisher browse surface where the visible UI would land.
